title: Measles Cases Hit New Record in U.S., as Vaccination Rates Wane
partialText: More measles cases have been reported in the United States in the last two years than in all the years from 2000 through 2024 combined.

title: The New Race to Find Treatments for Measles
partialText: As vaccination rates decline, biotech companies see a potential new market for measles drugs.

title: What to Know About Peptides the FDA Is Considering for Use
partialText: The agency is considering whether compounding pharmacies should be allowed to produce BPC-157, TB-500 and other previously banned peptides.

title: Crucial Interest Rate Jumps to Highest Level of Trump’s Second Term
partialText: The yield on the 10-year Treasury bond has risen steadily this year, as the Iran war rages, government spending worries intensify and artificial intelligence spending boosts growth.

title: Iran War and Trump’s Tariffs Threaten a Resilient U.S. Economy
partialText: As renewed fighting with Iran sends oil and gas prices soaring, President Trump has imposed new global tariffs that could push up prices further.

title: As Canada Opens Gordie Howe International Bridge, Americans Are Told to Stay Home
partialText: After a delay ordered by President Trump and new tariffs against Canada, the bridge between Windsor, Ontario, and Detroit opens in “underwhelming” fashion on Friday.

title: China Has Come Through Trump’s Trade War in a Good Position
partialText: Despite threats from President Trump, the overall average weighted tariff on Chinese goods remained about the same, and is now lower than countries like Brazil and Canada.

title: ‘We’re Trapped in Hell’: Iranians Say Life Is Put On Hold by Months of War
partialText: Devastated by cycles of violence and economic crisis, many are giving up on work and their futures as the United States batters Iran again.

title: Wildfires in France and Spain Drive Tens of Thousands From Their Homes
partialText: French officials ordered the evacuation of the Cap Ferret peninsula, a popular holiday destination. Fires west of Madrid were closing in on populated areas.

title: Faced With Heat and Wildfires, France Turns to Spain to Learn How to Cope
partialText: A French government delegation will travel to its southern neighbor to learn how it copes with long spells of hot weather.

title: C.D.C. Expands Cyclospora Outbreak Linked to Iceberg Lettuce to Nine States
partialText: Illinois, Kansas, Oklahoma and Pennsylvania now join Michigan, Ohio, Indiana, Kentucky and West Virginia in cyclospora outbreak linked to iceberg lettuce.

title: After the Cesar Chavez Scandal, Can Johnny Itliong Restore His Father’s Activist Legacy?
partialText: Johnny Itliong says Cesar Chavez stole credit from his father, the farmworker activist Larry Itliong. For years, he has been trying to correct the record.

title: How a Grieving Trump Decided to Back Lindsey Graham’s Sister for Senate
partialText: The president initially backed a little-known congressman. Then he talked to Gov. Henry McMaster and Ms. Graham herself.

title: Democrats Prepare for Possible Election Clashes With Federal Government
partialText: Top officials overseeing state elections and law enforcement are stepping up plans to prepare for what they worry could be interference in the midterms.

title: Can This New Enzyme Turn Back the Clock in Bodily Tissues?
partialText: In a recent study, scientists devised a way of reversing the buildup of compounds that lead to some age-related diseases.

title: Is the Amaury Family, Owners of the Tour de France, Hurting Cycling?
partialText: The Amaurys of Paris own the race, but won’t share any of the $170 million in media revenue. Sponsors and riders say their resistance is dooming the sport.

title: The Artist Matthew Taylor Is Helping Trump Reshape Washington
partialText: Matthew Taylor, a conceptual artist and political strategist, made influential ads and documentaries produced by Steve Bannon. Now he’s assisting the White House.

title: Argentines Facing Surge of Criticism After World Cup Loss Have Something to Say
partialText: Many Argentines condemned their players’ racist chants and aggressive behavior during the World Cup, but rejected what felt like a sweeping stigmatization of their entire nation.

title: 7th Time’s a Charm for a First-Time Buyer Plagued by Bidding Wars
partialText: Even as the market shifts to buyers, first-timers need to be resilient and flexible.

title: Eight Years Later, They’re Still Restoring a House Bought at Auction
partialText: First-time buyers from the Bay Area won an abandoned house at a Kingston, N.Y., tax auction. Eight years later, they’re still restoring it.

title: When Your First Apartment Is a Lemon
partialText: What New York homeowners can do before and after a purchase to avoid or mitigate shoddy construction.

title: I’m Native American. Land Acknowledgments Are Infuriating.
partialText: Conservatives who critique land acknowledgments aren’t acting in good faith, but they do have a point.

title: Help! I Might Be a Tradwife!
partialText: I’m not the target audience for online content about frontier chores and child-rearing. But if I’m honest, domestic rituals help to keep me sane.

title: A Big Day for Math
partialText: Yesterday was a big day for mathematics. We look at the winners of the Fields Medals.

title: Venezuela’s Earthquakes Show Wealth Divide, Even in Death
partialText: Latin America’s deep-seated inequalities prevailed over the grimly equalizing force of the Venezuela earthquakes, and set even the dead apart.
